A Layer Calculus for Agent-Authored Systems

Section titled “A Layer Calculus for Agent-Authored Systems”

Formal Technical Report · November 2026

Abstract

Section titled “Abstract”

Autonomous coding agents fail in three recurring ways. They leap from a requirement to code and invent the missing design; they lose the rationale for load-bearing choices and later weaken tests to make builds pass; and they leave humans with no trustworthy intermediate view of what the system does. This report presents a layer calculus that makes software development a sequence of verified behavior inclusions. A layer records intents, their support, design decisions, state machines, a decomposition into child contracts, and evidence. One relation — behavior inclusion under an abstraction map — serves for intent satisfaction, contract refinement, connector decomposition, and code realization. Stratification turns support evaluation into a forward recurrence, sibling verification into a substitution lemma, and version evolution into proof reuse at unchanged interfaces. The central theorem states that a valid stratified development refines the admitted root intents, conditional on explicit executable-realization and profile-admissibility premises. The report develops the layer definition, the soundness proof, the cutoff theorem, a five-gate agent protocol, a four-step evolution loop, and a complete durable-acknowledgement example, and it specifies a small mechanization target.

1. Introduction

Section titled “1. Introduction”

1.1 The problem

Section titled “1.1 The problem”

An agent is asked to add a feature or change a subsystem. It receives a requirement sentence and produces code. Between the sentence and the code lie decisions the sentence does not contain: data layout, ownership, error semantics, protocol ordering, retry policy, concurrency control, and edge-case handling. When the agent fills that gap in one leap, three failures follow.

Wide abstraction leap. The agent invents the missing design while writing the implementation. Implicit choices become hidden assumptions: a synchronous clock, a lossless channel, an atomic write that is not atomic, a lock that is not held across the operation that needs it. The resulting system can pass unit tests and still violate the requirement under interleaving, failure, or scale.

Rationale erasure and silent test weakening. A source repository records the final code, not the ordered argument for why a structure or protocol was chosen from upstream constraints, nor why the alternatives were rejected. A later agent cannot distinguish a load-bearing invariant from an incidental detail. Faced with a failing test, the cheapest repair is often to delete the assertion or weaken the condition. The build passes; the invariant is gone.

Human inscrutability. There is no trustworthy intermediate view. To know what the system does, a human must read thousands of lines of agent-generated code, reconstruct the design from the implementation, and guess which parts are intentional. Review degrades into rubber-stamping or line-by-line debugging.

1.2 Why post-hoc auditing does not address the problem

Section titled “1.2 Why post-hoc auditing does not address the problem”

An audit that runs after the code exists can detect some violations, but it does not prevent the leap that produced them. A diff algorithm can show what changed, but it cannot show which invariant the change was supposed to preserve. A test suite can encode a requirement, but a test is evidence about a sample, not a proof of a universal behavioral obligation, and it is exactly the artifact an agent can weaken. The problem is structural: the development process has no mandatory intermediate objects that are both behavioral and checkable.

1.3 The stratified thesis

Section titled “1.3 The stratified thesis”

Development proceeds through a persistent sequence of behavioral layers

L0⟶L1⟶⋯⟶LL⟶executable code.\mathcal{L}_0 \longrightarrow \mathcal{L}_1 \longrightarrow \cdots \longrightarrow \mathcal{L}_L \longrightarrow \text{executable code}.L0​⟶L1​⟶⋯⟶LL​⟶executable code.

At each layer kkk, the developer records:

  • the intents active at layer kkk and the support that activates them;
  • the design decisions taken at layer kkk, with their alternatives and reopening conditions;
  • explicit state machines for the components at layer kkk;
  • a decomposition of each component into child contracts for layer k+1k+1k+1;
  • evidence that the layer’s machines satisfy its intents and that its decomposition is sound.

A candidate advances only when the required checks at that layer succeed. Layer LLL is the executable layer: each leaf machine is realized by a program under a declared execution semantics. Stringent layer validity includes the operational realization of the wiring and the selected profile’s initialization, input, and progress conditions; the soundness theorem is conditional on them. The result is a chain of behavior inclusions, one layer at a time, where every link is small enough to verify and every link is retained as evidence.

The prevention claim is precise. An implementation that violates a protected, formally expressed obligation cannot be accepted by a sound gate whose complete dependencies are preserved. The gate does not make the agent intelligent; it makes the agent’s obligations explicit, local, ordered, and checkable.

1.4 Contributions

Section titled “1.4 Contributions”
  1. A layer calculus in which intent satisfaction, contract refinement, connector decomposition, and code realization are one relation: behavior inclusion.
  2. A stratified support recurrence with a separate evidence stratum and a protected-obligation preservation rule, so neither a failed check nor a support edit silently erases the obligation.
  3. A stratified soundness theorem whose chain is executable realization, connector monotonicity, child refinement, and inclusion transitivity.
  4. A sibling-independence theorem with explicit composition conditions, including interaction ownership and executable closure.
  5. A key-locality cutoff theorem: a change that preserves an interface reuses every ancestor proof by substitution.
  6. A five-gate development protocol and a four-step evolution loop, including a repair taxonomy that separates semantic counterexamples, failed proof witnesses, and unresolved checker results.
  7. A complete durable-acknowledgement example, worked through three layers, with a single-use interface precondition, a visible durability observation, leaf pseudocode, an agent error, its counterexample, and two repair paths.
  8. A mechanization target small enough to audit in one sitting.

1.5 Roadmap

Section titled “1.5 Roadmap”

Section 2 fixes the refinement algebra. Section 3 defines layers, support, decisions, validity, and proves stratified soundness. Section 4 details the four verification obligations and the evidence discipline. Section 5 treats decomposition, connectors, and sibling independence. Section 6 gives the development protocol. Section 7 gives versions, keys, cutoff, and evolution. Section 8 works the durable-acknowledgement example. Section 9 specifies the mechanization target. Sections 10–11 cover related work and open problems. The appendices record the finite probes that motivate the counterexamples and give proof details.

2. The Refinement Algebra

Section titled “2. The Refinement Algebra”

2.1 Observations, machines, and specifications

Section titled “2.1 Observations, machines, and specifications”

Fix an interface XXX. An observation space OX\mathcal{O}_XOX​ is a set of observations of XXX. The core instance is the set of finite traces over the visible actions of XXX; the liveness instance adds maximal traces under a declared fairness condition; the timed and probabilistic instances replace traces with timed or measure-valued observations. A specification at XXX is a subset Φ⊆OX\Phi \subseteq \mathcal{O}_XΦ⊆OX​.

A machine at XXX is a structure

M=(S,S0,Σ,→,obsM)M = (S, S_0, \Sigma, \to, \mathrm{obs}_M)M=(S,S0​,Σ,→,obsM​)

where SSS is a state set, S0⊆SS_0 \subseteq SS0​⊆S the initial states, Σ\SigmaΣ a partitioned alphabet of inputs, outputs, and internal actions, →⊆S×Σ×S\to \subseteq S \times \Sigma \times S→⊆S×Σ×S the transition relation, and obsM\mathrm{obs}_MobsM​ maps executions to observations. Its behavior is

beh⁡(M)={ obsM(ρ)∣ρ is an execution of M }⊆OX.\operatorname{beh}(M) = \{\, \mathrm{obs}_M(\rho) \mid \rho \text{ is an execution of } M \,\} \subseteq \mathcal{O}_X .beh(M)={obsM​(ρ)∣ρ is an execution of M}⊆OX​.

For the trace kernel, beh⁡(M)\operatorname{beh}(M)beh(M) is a trace set and is written tr⁡(M)\operatorname{tr}(M)tr(M).

2.2 Satisfaction, refinement, and abstraction

Section titled “2.2 Satisfaction, refinement, and abstraction”

Satisfaction and refinement are inclusion:

M⊨Φ  ⟺  beh⁡(M)⊆Φ,M⪯A  ⟺  beh⁡(M)⊆beh⁡(A).M \models \Phi \iff \operatorname{beh}(M) \subseteq \Phi, \qquad M \preceq A \iff \operatorname{beh}(M) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(A).M⊨Φ⟺beh(M)⊆Φ,M⪯A⟺beh(M)⊆beh(A).

With an abstraction map α:OX′→OX\alpha : \mathcal{O}_{X'} \to \mathcal{O}_Xα:OX′​→OX​,

M⪯αA  ⟺  α(beh⁡(M))⊆beh⁡(A),α∗Φ={ o′∈OX′∣α(o′)∈Φ }.M \preceq_\alpha A \iff \alpha(\operatorname{beh}(M)) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(A), \qquad \alpha^*\Phi = \{\, o' \in \mathcal{O}_{X'} \mid \alpha(o') \in \Phi \,\}.M⪯α​A⟺α(beh(M))⊆beh(A),α∗Φ={o′∈OX′​∣α(o′)∈Φ}.

(α2∘α1)∗=α1∗∘α2∗,id∗=id.(\alpha_2 \circ \alpha_1)^* = \alpha_1^* \circ \alpha_2^*, \qquad \mathrm{id}^* = \mathrm{id}.(α2​∘α1​)∗=α1∗​∘α2∗​,id∗=id.

2.3 Connectors

Section titled “2.3 Connectors”

A connector at a parent cell vvv is a map on behavior sets,

Kv:∏c∈ch⁡(v)P(OXc)⟶P(OXv),K_v : \prod_{c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)} \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{O}_{X_c}) \longrightarrow \mathcal{P}(\mathcal{O}_{X_v}),Kv​:c∈ch(v)∏​P(OXc​​)⟶P(OXv​​),

and it is admissible when it is monotone:

Bc⊆Bc′ for all c  ⟹  Kv({Bc}c)⊆Kv({Bc′}c).B_c \subseteq B'_c \text{ for all } c \;\Longrightarrow\; K_v(\{B_c\}_c) \subseteq K_v(\{B'_c\}_c).Bc​⊆Bc′​ for all c⟹Kv​({Bc​}c​)⊆Kv​({Bc′​}c​).

The operational reading is a wiring skeleton WvW_vWv​ that routes, synchronizes, interleaves, and hides child actions, with no state of its own that is not visible in the children or in a declared substrate primitive. A trajectory model of WvW_vWv​ supplies:

  • a set legal⁡Wv\operatorname{legal}_{W_v}legalWv​​ of legal shared trajectories rrr;
  • for each child ccc, a slice slice⁡c(r)\operatorname{slice}_c(r)slicec​(r) in OXc\mathcal{O}_{X_c}OXc​​;
  • a projection obs⁡v(r)\operatorname{obs}_v(r)obsv​(r) in OXv\mathcal{O}_{X_v}OXv​​.

The induced transformer is

Kv({Bc}c)={ obs⁡v(r)  ∣  legal⁡Wv(r) ∧ ∀c. slice⁡c(r)∈Bc }.K_v(\{B_c\}_c) = \bigl\{\, \operatorname{obs}_v(r) \;\big|\; \operatorname{legal}_{W_v}(r) \ \wedge\ \forall c.\ \operatorname{slice}_c(r) \in B_c \,\bigr\}.Kv​({Bc​}c​)={obsv​(r)​legalWv​​(r) ∧ ∀c. slicec​(r)∈Bc​}.

Lemma 1 (Trajectory connectors are monotone). If Bc⊆Bc′B_c \subseteq B'_cBc​⊆Bc′​ for every ccc, then Kv({Bc}c)⊆Kv({Bc′}c)K_v(\{B_c\}_c) \subseteq K_v(\{B'_c\}_c)Kv​({Bc​}c​)⊆Kv​({Bc′​}c​).

Proof. Take o∈Kv({Bc}c)o \in K_v(\{B_c\}_c)o∈Kv​({Bc​}c​). There is a legal rrr with obs⁡v(r)=o\operatorname{obs}_v(r) = oobsv​(r)=o and slice⁡c(r)∈Bc\operatorname{slice}_c(r) \in B_cslicec​(r)∈Bc​ for every ccc. Since Bc⊆Bc′B_c \subseteq B'_cBc​⊆Bc′​, each slice lies in Bc′B'_cBc′​ as well, so o∈Kv({Bc′}c)o \in K_v(\{B'_c\}_c)o∈Kv​({Bc′​}c​). ■\blacksquare■

The trajectory model is the mathematical content of the wiring. Its operational soundness obligation is that the implementation of WvW_vWv​ produces only observations in the transformer’s output. This is where routing, synchronization, initialization, and shared-resource behavior are established. It is a property of the connector, discharged once per wiring pattern, not a per-child obligation.

2.4 The single relation and its five uses

Section titled “2.4 The single relation and its five uses”

Every behavioral obligation in the calculus is an instance of inclusion:

Use Left side Right side Where checked
Satisfaction beh⁡(Mv)\operatorname{beh}(M_v)beh(Mv​) active intent Φ\PhiΦ layer kkk
Wiring adequacy Beh⁡(Cv[Qc])\operatorname{Beh}(C_v[Q_c])Beh(Cv​[Qc​]) Kv({αc(Qc)}c)K_v(\{\alpha_c(Q_c)\}_c)Kv​({αc​(Qc​)}c​) layer kkk, universally over admissible QcQ_cQc​
Decomposition Kv({Bv,c}c)K_v(\{B_{v,c}\}_c)Kv​({Bv,c​}c​) beh⁡(Mv)\operatorname{beh}(M_v)beh(Mv​) layer kkk
Refinement beh⁡(Mc)\operatorname{beh}(M_c)beh(Mc​) contract Bv,cB_{v,c}Bv,c​ layer k+1k+1k+1
Realization beh⁡(Pℓ)\operatorname{beh}(P_\ell)beh(Pℓ​) beh⁡(Mℓ)\operatorname{beh}(M_\ell)beh(Mℓ​) layer LLL

The algebra is small on purpose. The paper’s correctness argument is the transitive closure of this table, and the engineering content is the discipline that decides what to put on each side.

2.5 Semantic profiles

Section titled “2.5 Semantic profiles”

A semantic profile Γ\GammaΓ fixes the observation class and the obligations that accompany it:

  • Safety profile. Observations are finite visible traces; M⪯AM \preceq AM⪯A is trace inclusion.
  • Liveness profile. Observations are maximal traces under a declared fairness condition; refinement preserves maximality and fairness, and a progress obligation accompanies the trace inclusion.
  • Timed and probabilistic profiles. Observations are timed traces or path measures; refinement uses the corresponding measurable or timed preorder.

Two side conditions belong to every open-interface profile:

  • Input receptiveness. If a contract permits an input at a related state, the child must accept it. Without this condition, a child can satisfy a safety contract by refusing every request, which is not an admissible replacement.
  • Progress preservation. For a liveness contract, the child must preserve the required maximal fair executions. Finite-prefix inclusion alone admits a machine that accepts a request and then stops.

The core theorems are stated for the trace profile with these two side conditions. The timed and probabilistic instantiations use the same layer structure and the same schema; only the profile’s refinement relation and composition lemma change.

2.6 Boundary discipline

Section titled “2.6 Boundary discipline”

A contract constrains observable behavior at the child interface and the child’s duties to the connector. It may specify:

  • the inputs the child must accept;
  • the outputs it may produce and their order;
  • relations between its outputs and shared connector state;
  • progress or termination duties;
  • the environment assumptions under which those duties hold.

It does not prescribe the child’s internal algorithm, data layout, module structure, or implementation strategy. The child is free to choose any implementation whose behavior lies within the contract. This is the boundary rule that makes independent development possible: the parent owns the interface; the child owns the implementation.

3. Layers and Stratified Development

Section titled “3. Layers and Stratified Development”

3.1 The layer record

Section titled “3.1 The layer record”

A layer is a finite record

Lk=(Ik, Jk, Dk, Vk, χk, Ek).\mathcal{L}_k = \bigl(I_k,\ J_k,\ D_k,\ V_k,\ \chi_k,\ E_k\bigr).Lk​=(Ik​, Jk​, Dk​, Vk​, χk​, Ek​).

The fields have distinct roles.

IkI_kIk​ — intent records. A finite set of intents. Each c∈Ikc \in I_kc∈Ik​ carries:

  • a stable identifier id⁡(c)\operatorname{id}(c)id(c) and an exact content digest;
  • an owner cell owner⁡(c)∈Vk\operatorname{owner}(c) \in V_kowner(c)∈Vk​; an interaction-boundary label may annotate the owner for explanation, but the owner is always a cell;
  • a predicate ⟦c⟧⊆OXowner⁡(c)\llbracket c \rrbracket \subseteq \mathcal{O}_{X_{\operatorname{owner}(c)}}[[c]]⊆OXowner(c)​​;
  • an authority tag: root\mathrm{root}root, protected\mathrm{protected}protected, or delegated\mathrm{delegated}delegated.

A requirement that has no formal interpretation is recorded as an intent with a pending formalization status; it remains visible and blocks the obligations that depend on it. Ownership is total and unique: every active intent is owned by exactly one cell, so the per-cell required sets cover AkA_kAk​.

JkJ_kJk​ — support links. For each c∈Ikc \in I_kc∈Ik​, a finite set Jk(c)J_k(c)Jk​(c) of support groups. Each group P∈Jk(c)P \in J_k(c)P∈Jk​(c) is a finite set of references to earlier intents or earlier selected decisions, including contract selections. A group is conjunctive: all of its references must be active. Multiple groups are alternatives: any one suffices. The support link is provenance; when it claims logical entailment rather than an accepted design rationale, it carries a separate proof obligation.

DkD_kDk​ — decision records. A finite set of design decisions. Each decision d∈Dkd \in D_kd∈Dk​ has:

  • a question identifier q(d)q(d)q(d);
  • a selected option o(d)o(d)o(d);
  • a finite set alt⁡(d)\operatorname{alt}(d)alt(d) of rejected alternatives, each with an assessment and a reopening condition;
  • a finite prerequisite set prem⁡(d)\operatorname{prem}(d)prem(d) of references;
  • a rationale why⁡(d)\operatorname{why}(d)why(d);
  • a selection proposition sel⁡(q(d),o(d))\operatorname{sel}(q(d), o(d))sel(q(d),o(d));
  • a reopening predicate reopen⁡(d)\operatorname{reopen}(d)reopen(d) on the environment or version.

The ledger also carries a finite set NkN_kNk​ of nogoods: each nogood is a finite set of selection propositions that cannot all be true. A decision is evaluated independently: its prerequisites may mention the layer’s active intents and earlier layers’ selections, but not the selections of the same layer. After the layer’s decisions are evaluated, the joint consistency of SkS_kSk​ with the nogoods is checked. If two decisions need each other, they are placed at different layers or merged. This restriction is what keeps the recurrence a single pass.

VkV_kVk​ — cells. A finite set of components. Each cell v∈Vkv \in V_kv∈Vk​ owns:

  • an interface XvX_vXv​ and observation space OXv\mathcal{O}_{X_v}OXv​​;
  • a machine MvM_vMv​ at XvX_vXv​;
  • its active intents Φk(v)=⋂c∈Ak(v)⟦c⟧\Phi_k(v) = \bigcap_{c \in A_k(v)} \llbracket c \rrbracketΦk​(v)=⋂c∈Ak​(v)​[[c]], where Ak(v)⊆AkA_k(v) \subseteq A_kAk​(v)⊆Ak​ is the set of active intents owned by vvv;
  • a semantic context Γv\Gamma_vΓv​ (profile, fairness, environment assumptions).

χk\chi_kχk​ — decomposition or realization. For k<Lk < Lk<L, each non-leaf cell v∈Vkv \in V_kv∈Vk​ has a decomposition record

χk(v)=(Wv, ch⁡(v), (Bv,c)c∈ch⁡(v), αv),\chi_k(v) = \bigl(W_v,\ \operatorname{ch}(v),\ (B_{v,c})_{c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)},\ \alpha_v\bigr),χk​(v)=(Wv​, ch(v), (Bv,c​)c∈ch(v)​, αv​),

where WvW_vWv​ is a wiring skeleton, ch⁡(v)⊆Vk+1\operatorname{ch}(v) \subseteq V_{k+1}ch(v)⊆Vk+1​ is a finite set of child cells, Bv,cB_{v,c}Bv,c​ is the contract assigned to child ccc at its interface, and αv\alpha_vαv​ is the parent abstraction map. The children of the cells at layer kkk partition Vk+1V_{k+1}Vk+1​, and every cell at layer k<Lk < Lk<L has at least one child. A leaf is a cell at layer LLL; its decomposition record is a realization record. A cell that is already executable at layer kkk is represented by a trivial decomposition into a single child at layer k+1k+1k+1 with the same machine, repeated until layer LLL. Declaring a contract is a design decision and is recorded as a selection in DkD_kDk​; the support links of the next layer reference it through SkS_kSk​.

At k=Lk = Lk=L, χL(ℓ)\chi_L(\ell)χL​(ℓ) is a program PℓP_\ellPℓ​ together with an execution semantics for the leaf ℓ\ellℓ.

EkE_kEk​ — evidence. A finite map from obligation keys to evidence records. An evidence record carries the exact obligation, the method, the claim established, the result, the scope, and the artifact. Section 4.5 defines the validity condition. The evidence stratum is separate from the intent stratum: an intent’s activation does not depend on whether its evidence exists or passes.

3.2 Active intents and the support recurrence

Section titled “3.2 Active intents and the support recurrence”

Let SmS_mSm​ be the set of selection propositions of the decisions accepted at layer mmm. The active intents are computed top-down:

A0=I0root,A_0 = I_0^{\mathrm{root}},A0​=I0root​, Ak={ c∈Ik  ∣  ∃P∈Jk(c). P⊆⋃m=0k−1(Am∪Sm) }(1≤k≤L).A_k = \Bigl\{\, c \in I_k \;\Big|\; \exists P \in J_k(c).\ P \subseteq \bigcup_{m=0}^{k-1} \bigl(A_m \cup S_m\bigr) \,\Bigr\} \qquad (1 \le k \le L).Ak​={c∈Ik​​∃P∈Jk​(c). P⊆m=0⋃k−1​(Am​∪Sm​)}(1≤k≤L).

The recurrence has no fixed point. Support is strictly earlier-layer, so a single forward pass settles every layer. It is deterministic for a fixed candidate and costs the number of intent records, support groups, and premise occurrences.

The per-layer order is:

  1. compute AkA_kAk​ from the lower layers;
  2. resolve the decisions DkD_kDk​ against AkA_kAk​ and the earlier selections, and check consistency;
  3. verify the layer’s behavioral obligations;
  4. for k<Lk < Lk<L, declare the contracts that feed layer k+1k+1k+1, and record each declaration as a decision selection in DkD_kDk​.

Lemma 2 (Evidence separation). AkA_kAk​ is a function of (I,J,D,S)(I, J, D, S)(I,J,D,S) only. It does not mention EkE_kEk​. Consequently, a failed, missing, or pending evidence record leaves every obligation it concerns active.

Proof. The recurrence defining AkA_kAk​ refers only to intent records, support groups, and decision selections. The evidence stratum EkE_kEk​ does not occur in it. ■\blacksquare■

Lemma 2 is the anti-vacuity condition. If the gate defined the obligation set as “the intents whose evidence passes,” a failed requirement would disappear before it was checked, and the remaining set would be vacuously satisfied. The separation makes failure visible and blocking.

Corollary (No vacuous acceptance). A layer with an active, evidenced obligation whose evidence is absent or failing is not valid. The obligation remains in AkA_kAk​ and is reported as unsatisfied.

3.3 Decisions, selection, and consistency

Section titled “3.3 Decisions, selection, and consistency”

A decision is a provenance record, not a theorem. Its provenance validity is the prerequisite check:

prem⁡(d)⊆⋃m≤kAm∪⋃m<kSm\operatorname{prem}(d) \subseteq \bigcup_{m \le k} A_m \cup \bigcup_{m < k} S_mprem(d)⊆m≤k⋃​Am​∪m<k⋃​Sm​

for a decision at layer kkk. Its behavioral validity is checked separately: the machine or contract named by the selected option must satisfy the relevant behavioral obligations. The two checks are independent. A decision can be warranted while its chosen machine fails satisfaction; the gate catches the latter. A machine can satisfy its intents while the decision’s rationale is stale; the gate catches the former.

The set SkS_kSk​ is the set of selection propositions of accepted decisions at layer kkk. A decision is accepted when:

  1. its prerequisites are available;
  2. its selection is consistent with the nogoods introduced at layers ≤k\le k≤k and with the selections of lower layers;
  3. it is not marked stale.

The consistency condition is

∀n∈⋃m≤kNm.n⊈⋃m≤kSm.\forall n \in \bigcup_{m \le k} N_m.\quad n \not\subseteq \bigcup_{m \le k} S_m .∀n∈m≤k⋃​Nm​.n⊆m≤k⋃​Sm​.

A nogood whose selections span a later layer is not violated until those selections exist; the check at the later layer includes the earlier nogood. Because selection is explicit, there is no disjunctive closure to compute and no nonmonotonic inference to guard. A question with several acceptable options is represented by several decisions or by one decision with alternatives; exactly one selection is active. The rejected alternatives remain in the ledger, addressable by their reopening conditions, without entering the active semantics.

Staleness. If an intent, contract, or decision xxx changes, the decisions whose prerequisite closure contains xxx are stale:

stale⁡(x)={ d∣x∈prem⁡∗(d) }.\operatorname{stale}(x) = \{\, d \mid x \in \operatorname{prem}^*(d) \,\}.stale(x)={d∣x∈prem∗(d)}.

The prerequisite graph is acyclic because prerequisites are strictly earlier-layer or same-layer intents (not same-layer selections), so the reverse-reachable set is computed in linear time. A stale decision blocks publication of every layer in which it is a prerequisite of an active intent. Re-warranting it, or replacing it with a new decision and reopening its alternatives, is the repair.

A reopening predicate fires independently of premise changes. It is evaluated against the current environment and version. The predicate keeps rejected alternatives alive as first-class objects: when the condition that motivated the rejection no longer holds, the decision is stale and the alternative is reconsidered.

Section titled “3.4 Intra-layer validity”

Before the validity conditions, define the executable behavior of a sub-development. For a leaf ℓ\ellℓ, Beh⁡exec(ℓ)=beh⁡(Pℓ)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(\ell) = \operatorname{beh}(P_\ell)Behexec​(ℓ)=beh(Pℓ​) under the declared execution semantics. For a decomposed cell vvv, let CvC_vCv​ be the concrete wiring implementation and let Beh⁡exec(v)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v)Behexec​(v) be the set of observations CvC_vCv​ produces when it runs with the executable sub-developments of vvv‘s children under the declared substrate and scheduling semantics. The transformer KvK_vKv​ is the abstraction of CvC_vCv​: Beh⁡exec(v)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v)Behexec​(v) is the concrete object, and KvK_vKv​ is its specification-level image. Observation maps are typed: obs⁡c\operatorname{obs}_cobsc​ maps a child execution to OXc\mathcal{O}_{X_c}OXc​​, αc\alpha_cαc​ maps OXc\mathcal{O}_{X_c}OXc​​ to the contract interface, and obs⁡v\operatorname{obs}_vobsv​ maps a parent execution to OXv\mathcal{O}_{X_v}OXv​​; the maps compose through the refinement tree.

Lk\mathcal{L}_kLk​ is valid when seven conditions hold.

  1. Support well-formedness and ownership coverage. Every active intent in AkA_kAk​ has a support group whose references are available; the support links are acyclic; and the per-cell ownership sets cover the active set: ⋃v∈VkAk(v)=Ak,\bigcup_{v \in V_k} A_k(v) = A_k,v∈Vk​⋃​Ak​(v)=Ak​, with each active intent owned by exactly one cell.   2. Decision resolution. Every decision in DkD_kDk​ is accepted, and the selections are consistent with all nogoods introduced at layers ≤k\le k≤k and with lower layers.
  3. Satisfaction. For every cell v∈Vkv \in V_kv∈Vk​ and every active intent c∈Ak(v)c \in A_k(v)c∈Ak​(v), the evidence EkE_kEk​ contains a valid record for beh⁡(Mv)⊆⟦c⟧.\operatorname{beh}(M_v) \subseteq \llbracket c \rrbracket .beh(Mv​)⊆[[c]].
  4. Decomposition. For every non-leaf cell v∈Vkv \in V_kv∈Vk​ with χk(v)=(Wv,ch⁡(v),(Bv,c)c,αv)\chi_k(v) = (W_v, \operatorname{ch}(v), (B_{v,c})_c, \alpha_v)χk​(v)=(Wv​,ch(v),(Bv,c​)c​,αv​), the evidence EkE_kEk​ contains a valid record for Kv({beh⁡(Bv,c)}c∈ch⁡(v))⊆beh⁡(Mv),K_v\bigl(\{\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\}_{c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)}\bigr) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v),Kv​({beh(Bv,c​)}c∈ch(v)​)⊆beh(Mv​), where KvK_vKv​ is the transformer induced by WvW_vWv​ and αv\alpha_vαv​. Here beh⁡(Bv,c)\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})beh(Bv,c​) is the set of observations the contract permits; a contract is a specification and is read as a behavior set.
  5. Executable realization. For a decomposed cell vvv, the evidence EkE_kEk​ contains a wiring adequacy certificate for the concrete wiring CvC_vCv​: ∀(Qc)c∈ch⁡(v). (∀c. Qc is an admissible child behavior for Xc,Γc)⇒Beh⁡(Cv[Qc])⊆Kv({αc(Qc)}c).\forall (Q_c)_{c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)}.\ \Bigl(\forall c.\ Q_c \text{ is an admissible child behavior for } X_c,\Gamma_c\Bigr) \Rightarrow \operatorname{Beh}(C_v[Q_c]) \subseteq K_v\bigl(\{\alpha_c(Q_c)\}_{c}\bigr).∀(Qc​)c∈ch(v)​. (∀c. Qc​ is an admissible child behavior for Xc​,Γc​)⇒Beh(Cv​[Qc​])⊆Kv​({αc​(Qc​)}c​). The instance obligation is the specialization Qc=Beh⁡exec(c)Q_c = \operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(c)Qc​=Behexec​(c): Beh⁡exec(v)⊆Kv({αc(Beh⁡exec(c))}c∈ch⁡(v)),\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq K_v\bigl(\{\alpha_c(\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(c))\}_{c \in \operatorname{ch}(v)}\bigr),Behexec​(v)⊆Kv​({αc​(Behexec​(c))}c∈ch(v)​), derived by application of the universal certificate, not by a separate solver. Admissible here means the child behavior satisfies the interface typing, input-receptiveness, and profile conditions for Xc,ΓcX_c,\Gamma_cXc​,Γc​; condition 6 certifies that the executable child behaviors are admissible. This is the operational-soundness and interaction-completeness condition: the concrete wiring produces only observations admitted by its transformer and its children. For a leaf ℓ∈VL\ell \in V_Lℓ∈VL​, the evidence ELE_LEL​ contains a valid record for Beh⁡exec(ℓ)=beh⁡(Pℓ)⊆beh⁡(Mℓ),\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(\ell) = \operatorname{beh}(P_\ell) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_\ell),Behexec​(ℓ)=beh(Pℓ​)⊆beh(Mℓ​), and the leaf’s initial state set is nonempty under the declared initialization.
  6. Profile admissibility. The selected semantic profile’s conditions hold:
    • Initialization. Every initial state is in the invariant, and the initial state set is nonempty.
    • Input receptiveness. If a contract permits an input at a related state, the child accepts it.
    • Progress. For a liveness claim only, the required maximal fair executions are preserved under the declared fairness and enabling conditions. These conditions are part of validity, not background assumptions. They block the empty-behavior and request-refusal witnesses.

Conditions 5 and 6 are the executable premises that the soundness theorem consumes. Condition 7 is the anti-erasure premise that the publication gate consumes.

3.5 Inter-layer refinement

Section titled “3.5 Inter-layer refinement”

For k<Lk < Lk<L, the inter-layer operator is

Lk⇛Lk+1  ⟺  ∀v∈Vk. ∀c∈ch⁡(v). Ek+1 contains a valid record for beh⁡(Mc)⊆beh⁡(Bv,c) under αc.\mathcal{L}_k \Rrightarrow \mathcal{L}_{k+1} \iff \forall v \in V_k.\ \forall c \in \operatorname{ch}(v).\ E_{k+1} \text{ contains a valid record for } \operatorname{beh}(M_c) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c}) \text{ under } \alpha_c .Lk​⇛Lk+1​⟺∀v∈Vk​. ∀c∈ch(v). Ek+1​ contains a valid record for beh(Mc​)⊆beh(Bv,c​) under αc​.

The operator compares a child implementation with the contract its parent declared. It does not compare the new child with the old child; the contract is the complete interface. This is the ownership discipline in action. The operator’s conclusion is about the child machine; condition 5 carries it to the executable sub-development.

A stratified development of depth LLL is a sequence (L0,…,LL)(\mathcal{L}_0, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_L)(L0​,…,LL​) satisfying Lk⇛Lk+1\mathcal{L}_k \Rrightarrow \mathcal{L}_{k+1}Lk​⇛Lk+1​ for every k<Lk < Lk<L. It is valid when every layer is intra-layer valid and every adjacent pair satisfies the operator. It is complete when every layer is resolved (no pending decisions) and every required realization obligation is discharged.

3.6 Stratified soundness

Section titled “3.6 Stratified soundness”

Theorem 1 (Stratified soundness). Let (L0,…,LL)(\mathcal{L}_0, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_L)(L0​,…,LL​) be a stratified development. Suppose:

  • (A1) every layer is intra-layer valid (conditions 1–7 of §3.4);
  • (A2) Lk⇛Lk+1\mathcal{L}_k \Rrightarrow \mathcal{L}_{k+1}Lk​⇛Lk+1​ for every k<Lk < Lk<L;
  • (A3) the observation maps are typed and compose through the refinement tree.

Then for every kkk and every cell v∈Vkv \in V_kv∈Vk​, Beh⁡exec(v)⊆beh⁡(Mv)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v)Behexec​(v)⊆beh(Mv​), and for every active intent c∈Ak(v)c \in A_k(v)c∈Ak​(v), Beh⁡exec(v)⊆⟦c⟧\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq \llbracket c \rrbracketBehexec​(v)⊆[[c]]. In particular,

Beh⁡exec(v0)⊆Φ0(v0)=⋂c∈A0(v0)⟦c⟧,\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v_0) \subseteq \Phi_0(v_0) = \bigcap_{c \in A_0(v_0)} \llbracket c \rrbracket,Behexec​(v0​)⊆Φ0​(v0​)=c∈A0​(v0​)⋂​[[c]],

the semantic conjunction at the identified root v0v_0v0​, not the syntactic set A0A_0A0​.

Proof. Induct on L−kL - kL−k.

Base k=Lk = Lk=L. Condition 5 gives Beh⁡exec(ℓ)=beh⁡(Pℓ)⊆beh⁡(Mℓ)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(\ell) = \operatorname{beh}(P_\ell) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_\ell)Behexec​(ℓ)=beh(Pℓ​)⊆beh(Mℓ​) and the nonempty initial state condition. Condition 3 gives beh⁡(Mℓ)⊆⟦c⟧\operatorname{beh}(M_\ell) \subseteq \llbracket c \rrbracketbeh(Mℓ​)⊆[[c]] for every active intent ccc assigned to ℓ\ellℓ.

Step. Assume the claim for every child c∈ch⁡(v)⊆Vk+1c \in \operatorname{ch}(v) \subseteq V_{k+1}c∈ch(v)⊆Vk+1​, and write Bc=Beh⁡exec(c)B_c = \operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(c)Bc​=Behexec​(c). Let Bv,cB_{v,c}Bv,c​ be the contract declared by vvv for ccc. Condition 5 gives the universal wiring-adequacy certificate; instantiating it at Qc=BcQ_c = B_cQc​=Bc​, which is admissible by condition 6, gives the operational inclusion

Beh⁡exec(v)⊆Kv({αc(Bc)}c).(1)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq K_v\bigl(\{\alpha_c(B_c)\}_{c}\bigr). \qquad (1)Behexec​(v)⊆Kv​({αc​(Bc​)}c​).(1)

The induction hypothesis gives Bc⊆beh⁡(Mc)B_c \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_c)Bc​⊆beh(Mc​), hence αc(Bc)⊆αc(beh⁡(Mc))\alpha_c(B_c) \subseteq \alpha_c(\operatorname{beh}(M_c))αc​(Bc​)⊆αc​(beh(Mc​)). Monotonicity of KvK_vKv​ (Lemma 1) gives

Kv({αc(Bc)}c)⊆Kv({αc(beh⁡(Mc))}c).(2)K_v\bigl(\{\alpha_c(B_c)\}_{c}\bigr) \subseteq K_v\bigl(\{\alpha_c(\operatorname{beh}(M_c))\}_{c}\bigr). \qquad (2)Kv​({αc​(Bc​)}c​)⊆Kv​({αc​(beh(Mc​))}c​).(2)

The inter-layer operator (A2) gives αc(beh⁡(Mc))⊆beh⁡(Bv,c)\alpha_c(\operatorname{beh}(M_c)) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})αc​(beh(Mc​))⊆beh(Bv,c​). Monotonicity gives

Kv({αc(beh⁡(Mc))}c)⊆Kv({beh⁡(Bv,c)}c).(3)K_v\bigl(\{\alpha_c(\operatorname{beh}(M_c))\}_{c}\bigr) \subseteq K_v\bigl(\{\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\}_{c}\bigr). \qquad (3)Kv​({αc​(beh(Mc​))}c​)⊆Kv​({beh(Bv,c​)}c​).(3)

Condition 4 gives

Kv({beh⁡(Bv,c)}c)⊆beh⁡(Mv).(4)K_v\bigl(\{\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\}_{c}\bigr) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v). \qquad (4)Kv​({beh(Bv,c​)}c​)⊆beh(Mv​).(4)

Chaining (1)–(4) yields Beh⁡exec(v)⊆beh⁡(Mv)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v)Behexec​(v)⊆beh(Mv​). Condition 3 gives beh⁡(Mv)⊆⟦c⟧\operatorname{beh}(M_v) \subseteq \llbracket c \rrbracketbeh(Mv​)⊆[[c]] for every active intent ccc assigned to vvv. Condition 6 supplies the profile’s initialization, input, and progress conditions, so no step uses an empty behavior or a refused input to satisfy an obligation. The root case k=0k = 0k=0 gives Beh⁡exec(v0)⊆Φ0(v0)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v_0) \subseteq \Phi_0(v_0)Behexec​(v0​)⊆Φ0​(v0​). ■\blacksquare■

The proof is the whole spine. It uses executable realization, monotonicity, child refinement, decomposition, and transitivity. The stratification enters in the induction: every child’s proof is a separate premise, and the parent’s decomposition is checked against contracts rather than against the concrete product of child states. The operational counterexample — identity KKK, child {ok}\{ok\}{ok}, parent {ok}\{ok\}{ok}, actual wiring {bad}\{bad\}{bad} — is excluded by condition 5, because {bad}⊆{ok}\{bad\} \subseteq \{ok\}{bad}⊆{ok} is false. The empty-initial-state counterexample is excluded by condition 6.

3.7 Layer soundness and inspection

Section titled “3.7 Layer soundness and inspection”

Corollary 1 (Inspection is sound). For every kkk and v∈Vkv \in V_kv∈Vk​, Beh⁡exec(v)⊆beh⁡(Mv)⊆Φk(v)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v) \subseteq \Phi_k(v)Behexec​(v)⊆beh(Mv​)⊆Φk​(v). The inspection direction is: every executable behavior maps under the abstraction to a behavior permitted by the layer’s machines, and every universal obligation displayed at layer kkk transfers to the code. The converse does not hold: a layer may deliberately admit abstract behavior that the current implementation does not realize. For example, beh⁡(code)={a}\operatorname{beh}(\text{code}) = \{a\}beh(code)={a} and beh⁡(model)={a,b}\operatorname{beh}(\text{model}) = \{a,b\}beh(model)={a,b} satisfy refinement, yet bbb is abstractly permitted and concretely impossible. The layer is an abstraction, not a claim of behavioral equivalence.

The inspection view of layer kkk contains:

  • the active intents AkA_kAk​, with their support links and authority tags;
  • the decision ledger DkD_kDk​, with questions, selections, rejected alternatives, and reopening conditions;
  • the cells VkV_kVk​ and their machines MvM_vMv​;
  • the incoming contracts Bpar(v),vB_{\mathrm{par}(v),v}Bpar(v),v​ that each cell must refine;
  • the outgoing decomposition χk(v)\chi_k(v)χk​(v) that each non-leaf cell declares;
  • the evidence status EkE_kEk​: pass, fail, unresolved, pending, missing, and the scope of each method.

A human inspecting layer kkk sees what the system does, what it must do, why it is built this way, and that the view is a sound abstraction. They read code only to audit a specific leaf whose contract they already understand.

3.8 Protected obligation preservation

Section titled “3.8 Protected obligation preservation”

Define the effective protected inventory of a version GGG:

Prot⁡(G)={(id⁡(c),⟦c⟧,owner⁡(c),scope⁡(c)):c is active in G and authority⁡(c)∈{root,protected}}.\operatorname{Prot}(G) = \bigl\{(\operatorname{id}(c), \llbracket c \rrbracket, \operatorname{owner}(c), \operatorname{scope}(c)) : c \text{ is active in } G \text{ and } \operatorname{authority}(c) \in \{\mathrm{root}, \mathrm{protected}\}\bigr\}.Prot(G)={(id(c),[[c]],owner(c),scope(c)):c is active in G and authority(c)∈{root,protected}}.

A candidate G′G'G′ preserves GGG when for every p∈Prot⁡(G)p \in \operatorname{Prot}(G)p∈Prot(G), either ppp is active in G′G'G′ with the same semantic content, or an authorized disposition d∈AG′d \in \mathcal{A}_{G'}d∈AG′​ records ppp, the authorization, the reason, and the affected decisions. A support edit, ownership change, selection change, or interpretation change that removes ppp without such a disposition is rejected by validity condition 7. Ownership is total, so Prot⁡(G)\operatorname{Prot}(G)Prot(G) and the per-cell satisfaction sets range over the same active obligations; a protected interaction intent is assigned to the cell that owns the interaction boundary and is checked there.

The support-only witness: a protected intent ccc at layer 1 has J1(c)={{s}}J_1(c) = \{\{s\}\}J1​(c)={{s}} and sss is accepted. The candidate changes only J1(c)J_1(c)J1​(c) to ∅\emptyset∅. The identifier, predicate, authority tag, and selection are unchanged, but A1A_1A1​ loses ccc, so its satisfaction evidence is no longer requested. Condition 7 rejects the candidate; only an authorized disposition can retire ccc. Evidence failure does not deactivate an intent (Lemma 2), and a support or ownership edit does not deactivate a protected intent without a disposition (condition 7).

4. Verification Obligations

Section titled “4. Verification Obligations”

4.1 Satisfaction

Section titled “4.1 Satisfaction”

For a finite machine MvM_vMv​ and a specification Φ\PhiΦ, satisfaction is checked by exhaustive state-space exploration or by a certified invariant. For an infinite machine, it is checked by a theorem, a certified abstraction, or a bounded argument whose scope is recorded. The obligation is exactly

beh⁡(Mv)⊆Φ.\operatorname{beh}(M_v) \subseteq \Phi .beh(Mv​)⊆Φ.

A test is not, by itself, evidence for this universal inclusion. It is evidence for a bounded claim: no violation in the tested sample, or no violation within a bound. The evidence record must state the claim; the gate checks that the claim covers the obligation. A universal obligation is not discharged by a sampled test. A bounded intent can be discharged by a bounded check, provided the intent is stated with the same bound.

4.2 Decomposition and connector admissibility

Section titled “4.2 Decomposition and connector admissibility”

The decomposition obligation is

Kv({beh⁡(Bv,c)}c)⊆beh⁡(Mv).K_v\bigl(\{\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\}_{c}\bigr) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v).Kv​({beh(Bv,c​)}c​)⊆beh(Mv​).

It is checked at the parent layer, against the abstract contracts, not against the concrete children. The connector’s admissibility has four parts:

  1. Monotonicity. Lemma 1 for the trajectory model; definitional for any transformer presented as a monotone map.
  2. Operational soundness. The concrete wiring’s observations are contained in the transformer’s output. Routing, synchronization, initialization, and shared-resource behavior are covered by the trajectory model.
  3. Interaction ownership. Every inter-child synchronization action and every piece of shared state is owned by the wiring or by a declared substrate service. Children have pairwise disjoint private state. A stateful coordinator is a child cell with its own machine and eventual realization, not an unimplemented oracle inside the connector.
  4. Observation preservation under reduction. When concrete interleavings are replaced by the transformer’s compositional abstraction, the reduction preserves the observations of the profile. Transaction reduction and linearizability are proof methods for this condition when they apply; they are not mandatory ceremony for sequential components.

The wiring-adequacy certificate (parts 1–2) is what the soundness proof consumes; it is validity condition 5, and profile admissibility is condition 6. A layer without them is not valid, and Theorem 1 does not apply. The last two parts are what make the proof applicable to a real concurrent implementation. A connector that fails part 3 or 4 is outside the calculus until the missing owner or the reduction proof is supplied.

4.3 Child refinement

Section titled “4.3 Child refinement”

A child refinement obligation is

beh⁡(Mc)⊆αbeh⁡(Bv,c).\operatorname{beh}(M_c) \subseteq_\alpha \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c}).beh(Mc​)⊆α​beh(Bv,c​).

For finite trace inclusion, an inductive simulation witness establishes it:

  • an invariant Ic⊆SMcI_c \subseteq S_{M_c}Ic​⊆SMc​​;
  • a relation Rc⊆SMc×SBv,cR_c \subseteq S_{M_c} \times S_{B_{v,c}}Rc​⊆SMc​​×SBv,c​​;
  • an abstraction map λc\lambda_cλc​ from child actions to contract actions or silent steps.

The conditions are:

  1. Initiation. Every initial child state is in IcI_cIc​ and is related to an initial contract state.
  2. Consecution. IcI_cIc​ is closed under the child’s transitions.
  3. Step simulation. For (s,t)∈Rc(s, t) \in R_c(s,t)∈Rc​ and s→σs′s \xrightarrow{\sigma} s'sσ​s′: if λc(σ)=ϵ\lambda_c(\sigma) = \epsilonλc​(σ)=ϵ, then (s′,t)∈Rc(s', t) \in R_c(s′,t)∈Rc​; otherwise there is t′t't′ with t→λc(σ)t′t \xrightarrow{\lambda_c(\sigma)} t'tλc​(σ)​t′ and (s′,t′)∈Rc(s', t') \in R_c(s′,t′)∈Rc​.
  4. Input receptiveness. Every contract input enabled at ttt is enabled by some child input in λc−1\lambda_c^{-1}λc−1​ at sss.
  5. Silent convergence. For a liveness profile, a well-founded rank strictly decreases on silent steps, preventing infinite internal stuttering.

Lemma 3 (Finite-trace simulation). Conditions 1–3 imply λc(tr⁡(Mc))⊆tr⁡(Bv,c)\lambda_c(\operatorname{tr}(M_c)) \subseteq \operatorname{tr}(B_{v,c})λc​(tr(Mc​))⊆tr(Bv,c​).

Proof. Induct on the length of a child execution. Initiation relates the initial states. Consecution keeps the invariant. A silent step keeps the contract state; a visible step appends the matched contract transition. Every finite prefix therefore has a matching contract execution. ■\blacksquare■

For state-labeled properties, related states agree on the abstract valuations and silent steps preserve them. For liveness, the witness additionally preserves maximality and fairness, and validity condition 6 supplies the progress rank. For open inputs, simulation condition 4 blocks the trivial refusal strategy.

4.4 Realization

Section titled “4.4 Realization”

At layer LLL, each leaf has a program PℓP_\ellPℓ​ and an execution semantics. The obligation is

beh⁡(Pℓ)⊆beh⁡(Mℓ)\operatorname{beh}(P_\ell) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_\ell)beh(Pℓ​)⊆beh(Mℓ​)

under the declared semantics and environment assumptions. The leaf machine’s transitions are deterministic conditional on their explicit inputs; residual environment choices are explicit inputs or explicit semantic nondeterminism. The substrate contract names what the runtime guarantees: an atomic write, a flush completion, a message delivery, a clock granularity. The realization obligation is where those guarantees enter the proof. For a decomposed cell, realization is the universal wiring-adequacy certificate of §3.4: ∀Qc. Beh⁡(Cv[Qc])⊆Kv({αc(Qc)}c)\forall Q_c.\ \operatorname{Beh}(C_v[Q_c]) \subseteq K_v(\{\alpha_c(Q_c)\}_c)∀Qc​. Beh(Cv​[Qc​])⊆Kv​({αc​(Qc​)}c​) over admissible child behaviors; the instance Beh⁡exec(v)⊆Kv({αc(Beh⁡exec(c))}c)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq K_v(\{\alpha_c(\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(c))\}_c)Behexec​(v)⊆Kv​({αc​(Behexec​(c))}c​) follows by application. For a leaf, it is the program-to-machine inclusion above.

4.5 Evidence discipline

Section titled “4.5 Evidence discipline”

An evidence record for an obligation ooo is a tuple

e=(o, method, claim, result, scope, artifact).e = (o,\ \mathrm{method},\ \mathrm{claim},\ \mathrm{result},\ \mathrm{scope},\ \mathrm{artifact}).e=(o, method, claim, result, scope, artifact).

It is valid for ooo when:

  1. claim\mathrm{claim}claim is at least as strong as ooo;
  2. method\mathrm{method}method is sound for claim\mathrm{claim}claim under scope\mathrm{scope}scope;
  3. result\mathrm{result}result is pass.

The result field is one of {pass,fail,unresolved,pending}\{\mathrm{pass}, \mathrm{fail}, \mathrm{unresolved}, \mathrm{pending}\}{pass,fail,unresolved,pending}. Only pass discharges an obligation; unresolved and pending are not passes and cannot enter the Verified outcome.

The method determines the claim:

Method Claim it can establish What it cannot establish
Proof derivation the exact obligation nothing beyond the logic’s soundness
Exhaustive finite model check the obligation for the modeled machine adequacy of the model to the code
Bounded model check the obligation up to the bound the unbounded obligation
Property-based test no violation in the sampled domain a universal inclusion
Runtime monitor no violation in the observed run future or unobserved behavior
Translation validation the specific program-to-machine relation unrelated properties

The scope records the observation profile, machine class, environment assumptions, and any bound. A result is meaningful only within its scope.

4.6 Evidence separation and the three-gate structure

Section titled “4.6 Evidence separation and the three-gate structure”

Every layer has three independent gates:

  • Provenance gate. Every decision is accepted, its prerequisites hold, its selection is consistent, and no load-bearing decision is stale.
  • Behavioral gate. Every active intent has valid satisfaction evidence; every decomposition has valid evidence; every child has valid refinement evidence; every executable cell has valid realization evidence (wiring adequacy for a non-leaf cell, program-to-machine for a leaf); the profile’s initialization, input, and (where claimed) progress conditions hold.
  • Preservation gate. Every protected obligation in the previous version’s effective inventory remains active with the same semantic content, or an authorized disposition records its retirement or weakening. A support, ownership, selection, or interpretation edit that deactivates a protected obligation is rejected.

The separation matters. A failing behavioral check does not remove the intent from AkA_kAk​ (Lemma 2). A failing provenance check does not silently delete a machine. A support-only edit cannot deactivate a protected obligation without a disposition (condition 7). All failures are reported with their obligations, their evidence status, and the relevant witnesses. The version is not published until all three gates pass.

4.7 What the gate guarantees

Section titled “4.7 What the gate guarantees”

The gate guarantees that the published executable system refines the active root intents under the declared observation profile and substrate semantics. The guarantee is conditional on validity conditions 5 and 6 (executable realization and profile admissibility) and on the preservation condition 7, and it is relative to:

  • the admitted root intents and their authority;
  • the semantic profile and the environment assumptions;
  • the soundness of the evidence checkers;
  • the connector admissibility proofs;
  • the declared execution semantics of the leaf programs.

These are the theorem’s hypotheses, not disclaimers. The next section makes the composition conditions explicit.

5. Decomposition and Interaction

Section titled “5. Decomposition and Interaction”

5.1 Contracts are relational

Section titled “5.1 Contracts are relational”

A contract that constrains each child separately cannot express a correlation between children. The canonical witness is a parent that admits only the diagonal outcomes.

Proposition 1 (Coordinate projections erase correlation). Let the parent admit the outcome set R={(0,0),(1,1)}R = \{(0,0), (1,1)\}R={(0,0),(1,1)} over outputs (x,y)(x,y)(x,y). The coordinate projections are π1(R)={0,1}\pi_1(R) = \{0,1\}π1​(R)={0,1} and π2(R)={0,1}\pi_2(R) = \{0,1\}π2​(R)={0,1}. Two children that independently refine the projections can jointly emit (0,1)∉R(0,1) \notin R(0,1)∈/R.

Proof. {0,1}×{0,1}\{0,1\} \times \{0,1\}{0,1}×{0,1} contains (0,1)(0,1)(0,1), which is not in RRR. ■\blacksquare■

The remedy is one of two moves: make the contract relational (a relation between child observations and shared connector state), or hoist the correlation into the connector’s wiring. The calculus supports both. The point is that the parent layer must own the correlation; it cannot be pushed into independent child proofs.

5.2 Sibling independence

Section titled “5.2 Sibling independence”

Theorem 2 (Sibling independence). Fix a parent cell v∈Vkv \in V_kv∈Vk​ with children ch⁡(v)⊆Vk+1\operatorname{ch}(v) \subseteq V_{k+1}ch(v)⊆Vk+1​, contracts (Bv,c)c(B_{v,c})_c(Bv,c​)c​, wiring WvW_vWv​, and parent machine MvM_vMv​. Suppose:

  1. Child refinement. For every ccc, beh⁡(Mc)⊆αcbeh⁡(Bv,c)\operatorname{beh}(M_c) \subseteq_{\alpha_c} \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})beh(Mc​)⊆αc​​beh(Bv,c​), with input receptiveness and progress preservation under the profile.
  2. Connector monotonicity. The transformer KvK_vKv​ induced by WvW_vWv​ is monotone.
  3. Decomposition. Kv({beh⁡(Bv,c)}c)⊆beh⁡(Mv)K_v(\{\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\}_c) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v)Kv​({beh(Bv,c​)}c​)⊆beh(Mv​).
  4. Applicability. The wiring’s operational realization is sound for KvK_vKv​; interaction ownership and reduction preservation hold as required by the profile.

Then

Kv({αc(beh⁡(Mc))}c)⊆beh⁡(Mv),K_v\bigl(\{\alpha_c(\operatorname{beh}(M_c))\}_c\bigr) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(M_v),Kv​({αc​(beh(Mc​))}c​)⊆beh(Mv​),

without constructing the concrete sibling product ∏cSMc\prod_c S_{M_c}∏c​SMc​​.

Proof. Apply the abstraction maps to the child refinements, then apply monotonicity to get Kv({αc(beh⁡(Mc))}c)⊆Kv({beh⁡(Bv,c)}c)K_v(\{\alpha_c(\operatorname{beh}(M_c))\}_c) \subseteq K_v(\{\operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})\}_c)Kv​({αc​(beh(Mc​))}c​)⊆Kv​({beh(Bv,c​)}c​), and compose with the decomposition. ■\blacksquare■

The theorem is the step case of Theorem 1, stated separately because it is the engineering claim. The children are verified against their contracts, never against each other. The cost of the parent check is the abstract boundary, not the concrete product.

5.3 Executable closure

Section titled “5.3 Executable closure”

A connector that performs stateful coordination cannot remain an unimplemented mathematical object. The calculus requires:

  • the wiring WvW_vWv​ owns only the specified composition mechanism: routing, synchronizing, interleaving, hiding;
  • any stateful coordinator is a child cell with its own machine, contract, and eventual realization;
  • any custom router, scheduler, or runtime adapter introduced by the implementation receives its own realization obligation or becomes an explicit substrate assumption;
  • no action disappears between the mathematical composition and the executable delivery.

This rule closes the gap that otherwise lets an agent write a beautiful abstract connector and never implement it. The coordinator is refined like everything else.

5.4 Shared services

Section titled “5.4 Shared services”

A service used by several branches is declared at the lowest common ancestor uuu as an abstract atomic contract OabsO^{\mathrm{abs}}Oabs in the ambient context. Clients invoke it atomically without widening the intermediate interfaces. The service is implemented once, as a separate subtree, and proved to refine OabsO^{\mathrm{abs}}Oabs: linearizability for safety, a progress property for liveness. This is a factoring rule, not a new judgment. A stateless both-mover service (logging, telemetry) is an admissible connector with trivial state; its certificates establish the required commutation and progress.

5.5 Contract factoring and capacity

Section titled “5.5 Contract factoring and capacity”

A contract boundary can move history into the child and keep the connector small. With mmm idempotent resource bits and the invariant “not all mmm are held,” a naive joint recognizer needs 2m2^m2m states. With per-child two-state contracts that emit signed changes only on a genuine bit change, a connector that counts holders needs m+1m+1m+1 states. The gain is architectural: the connector’s state is small, and the history lives in the children. The bound is not a universal polynomial claim; the abstract boundary can still contain a product of contract states when the architecture requires it. The point is to choose the boundary so that the product is small.

5.6 Applicability conditions

Section titled “5.6 Applicability conditions”

The sibling-independence theorem is only as strong as its applicability conditions. The paper states them in the main text because they are the load-bearing assumptions:

  • Interaction ownership. Every shared interaction has an owning boundary; children have disjoint private state.
  • Operational soundness. The wiring model covers actual routing, synchronization, initialization, and shared-resource behavior.
  • Input and progress. The profile’s input receptiveness and progress obligations are preserved by the child refinement.
  • Reduction preservation. When interleavings are reduced, the reduction preserves the observations of the profile.

A connector that fails one of these is outside the calculus. The failure is a proof obligation, not a silent assumption.

6. The Development Protocol

Section titled “6. The Development Protocol”

6.1 The five gates

Section titled “6.1 The five gates”

The protocol is the operational reading of validity. An agent may publish a version only when all five gates pass.

G1 — Read the layer (process duty). Before proposing a change at layer kkk, the agent reads the layer’s active intents, support links, decisions, cells, incoming contracts, outgoing decomposition, and evidence status. This is a process obligation on the agent; G2–G5 are checked by the gate.

G2 — No abstraction skip. A machine at layer k+1k+1k+1 is introduced only as a child of a contract already declared in some χk(v)\chi_k(v)χk​(v). The agent cannot write layer k+1k+1k+1 code without first fixing the interface it must satisfy. This is the direct block on the wide abstraction leap.

G3 — Evidence required. Acceptance of a cell requires valid satisfaction evidence for every active intent assigned to it and valid executable-realization evidence: for a non-leaf cell, the universal wiring-adequacy certificate of condition 5; for a leaf, the program-to-machine inclusion. A non-leaf cell also requires valid decomposition evidence. Acceptance of a child requires valid refinement evidence. A test is evidence only for the claim it can establish. A weakened test weakens the claim, not the obligation; the universal obligation remains active and unsatisfied.

G4 — No silent specification weakening. Root and protected intents and contracts can be changed only through an authorized revision that creates a new version and reopens the dependent decisions. The agent may propose a revision; it cannot apply one as part of a code change. A support, ownership, selection, or interpretation edit that deactivates a protected obligation counts as a specification weakening and requires an authorized disposition. The authorization record is part of the version.

G5 — Atomic publication. A version is published only when every obligation in the affected dependency cone has valid pass evidence. Partial layers are not publishable. Missing, unresolved, or pending evidence is not a pass, and a failed local verification cannot be hidden by a successful build elsewhere.

6.2 The authoring cycle

Section titled “6.2 The authoring cycle”

The agent’s per-layer cycle is:

  1. Read. Load the layer’s inspection view and the incoming contracts.
  2. Decide. For each open design question, record a decision with its prerequisites, alternatives, rationale, and reopening condition. A decision that changes a protected item requires an authorized revision.
  3. Model. Propose the layer’s cells and their machines. Each machine must satisfy the active intents assigned to its cell.
  4. Decompose. For each non-leaf cell, declare the wiring and the child contracts, and discharge the decomposition and wiring-adequacy obligations.
  5. Assign. Hand each child contract to the next layer’s development. The child may be developed independently within its contract.
  6. Substitute. When a child is complete, substitute its refinement proof into the parent’s decomposition. Close the parent only when all children are discharged.

A locally checked design with unresolved descendants remains a development candidate. The completed-system gate quantifies over all required cells, decompositions, and executable artifacts.

6.3 What the agent may and may not change

Section titled “6.3 What the agent may and may not change”
Artifact Agent may Agent may not
Delegated intent refine, strengthen, or add a child intent delete or deactivate it via a support/ownership edit without an authorized revision
Protected intent propose a revision with rationale and reopening apply the revision, or deactivate it via a support/ownership edit, without an authorized disposition
Root intent implement it silently weaken, reinterpret, or deactivate it
Contract refine the child implementation; propose a contract revision change the contract to make a failing child pass
Decision add, re-warrant, or reopen with rationale erase the alternatives or the rationale
Machine choose any implementation within the contract declare a contract that the parent decomposition does not support
Evidence add evidence for the exact obligation substitute a weaker claim for a stronger obligation

6.4 Test weakening, intent revision, and authority

Section titled “6.4 Test weakening, intent revision, and authority”

The test-weakening failure is blocked at the evidence layer. A test is a decision procedure for a bounded or sampled claim. It cannot discharge a universal inclusion unless it is exhaustive for the relevant finite domain. If the agent deletes an assertion, the remaining test establishes a weaker claim; the universal obligation is still active, and the gate reports it as unsatisfied. The only way to remove the obligation is to change its intent, which requires an authorized revision and reopens the dependent decisions. A support, ownership, selection, or interpretation edit that removes a protected obligation is a removal even when the predicate bytes are unchanged; it requires the same authorized disposition.

The authority tags make this concrete:

  • Root intents are admitted by the owner at version creation.
  • Protected intents and contracts require an explicit authorization record to change.
  • Delegated intents may be refined by the agent within the protected boundary.

The authorization record is not a separate governance layer. It is a field of the version, checked by the same gate.

6.5 A transcript of a caught error

Section titled “6.5 A transcript of a caught error”
  1. The requirement says: acknowledge a request only after its result is durable.
  2. The agent writes a store that emits committed after write returns.
  3. The refinement check for the store contract returns the trace append, committed with no flush_ok/fsync.
  4. The evidence record is fail. The store contract remains active.
  5. The agent either adds the flush before committed (downward repair at the code layer) or, if the substrate cannot support the required durability, introduces a supported flush protocol and implements it, or obtains an authorized revision of the substrate/requirement premise and reopens the store decision.
  6. The version is published only after the new evidence passes and the reopen path is recorded.

The next section gives the full example.

7. Persistent Versions and Evolution

Section titled “7. Persistent Versions and Evolution”

7.1 Versions

Section titled “7.1 Versions”

A version is an immutable snapshot

Gt=(L0(t),…,LL(t), At),G_t = \bigl(\mathcal{L}_0^{(t)}, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_L^{(t)},\ \mathcal{A}_t\bigr),Gt​=(L0(t)​,…,LL(t)​, At​),

where At\mathcal{A}_tAt​ is the authorization record for protected revisions. The snapshot is identified by the hash of its canonical encoding. Publication is a compare-and-swap on the head pointer: a candidate Gt+1G_{t+1}Gt+1​ is installed only if the head still identifies GtG_tGt​. The persistent store — a content-addressed DAG, a Merkle trie, or a plain immutable map — is an implementation choice. The mathematical content of persistence is the locality of obligation keys.

7.2 Obligation keys

Section titled “7.2 Obligation keys”

Each obligation has a key that contains every semantic input to it and nothing else:

κWire(v)=h(Wire, Cv, Kv, αv, (αc)c, Γv, (Γc)c),κSat(v,c)=h(Sat, Mv, ⟦c⟧, Γv),κDec(v)=h(Dec, Wv, (Bv,c)c, Mv, αv, Γv),κRef(c)=h(Ref, Mc, Bpar(c),c, αc, Γc),κImpl(ℓ)=h(Impl, Pℓ, Mℓ, Γℓ).\begin{aligned} \kappa_{\mathrm{Wire}}(v) &= h\bigl(\text{Wire},\ C_v,\ K_v,\ \alpha_v,\ (\alpha_c)_c,\ \Gamma_v,\ (\Gamma_c)_c\bigr), \\ \kappa_{\mathrm{Sat}}(v, c) &= h\bigl(\text{Sat},\ M_v,\ \llbracket c \rrbracket,\ \Gamma_v\bigr), \\ \kappa_{\mathrm{Dec}}(v) &= h\bigl(\text{Dec},\ W_v,\ (B_{v,c})_c,\ M_v,\ \alpha_v,\ \Gamma_v\bigr), \\ \kappa_{\mathrm{Ref}}(c) &= h\bigl(\text{Ref},\ M_c,\ B_{\mathrm{par}(c),c},\ \alpha_c,\ \Gamma_c\bigr), \\ \kappa_{\mathrm{Impl}}(\ell) &= h\bigl(\text{Impl},\ P_\ell,\ M_\ell,\ \Gamma_\ell\bigr). \end{aligned}κWire​(v)κSat​(v,c)κDec​(v)κRef​(c)κImpl​(ℓ)​=h(Wire, Cv​, Kv​, αv​, (αc​)c​, Γv​, (Γc​)c​),=h(Sat, Mv​, [[c]], Γv​),=h(Dec, Wv​, (Bv,c​)c​, Mv​, αv​, Γv​),=h(Ref, Mc​, Bpar(c),c​, αc​, Γc​),=h(Impl, Pℓ​, Mℓ​, Γℓ​).​

The key never contains a storage pointer, a subtree hash, or a child implementation that is not a semantic input. Two equal keys denote the same obligation proposition; collisions are resolved by exact comparison of the encoded arguments.

7.3 Cutoff by proof substitution

Section titled “7.3 Cutoff by proof substitution”

Theorem 3 (Cutoff). Let GtG_tGt​ be a valid version. Replace the sub-development rooted at a child c∈Vk+1c \in V_{k+1}c∈Vk+1​ with a new sub-development. Keep fixed the contract Bv,cB_{v,c}Bv,c​, the wiring WvW_vWv​, the parent machine MvM_vMv​, the parent’s active intents, the parent abstraction map αv\alpha_vαv​, the child abstraction maps (αc)c(\alpha_c)_c(αc​)c​, the child contexts (Γc)c(\Gamma_c)_c(Γc​)c​, and every sibling. Suppose the new child sub-development is valid and satisfies

beh⁡(Mc′)⊆beh⁡(Bv,c)\operatorname{beh}(M'_c) \subseteq \operatorname{beh}(B_{v,c})beh(Mc′​)⊆beh(Bv,c​)

under the same profile and abstraction map αc\alpha_cαc​. Then every obligation at layers ≤k\le k≤k whose key does not mention the changed objects has an unchanged key and retains its evidence. In particular:

  • κWire(v)\kappa_{\mathrm{Wire}}(v)κWire​(v), κDec(v)\kappa_{\mathrm{Dec}}(v)κDec​(v), and κSat(v,c′)\kappa_{\mathrm{Sat}}(v, c')κSat​(v,c′) are unchanged for every parent intent c′c'c′;
  • every sibling κRef(c′)\kappa_{\mathrm{Ref}}(c')κRef​(c′) is unchanged;
  • the changed keys are confined to the replaced sub-development: κImpl(ℓ)\kappa_{\mathrm{Impl}}(\ell)κImpl​(ℓ) for a changed leaf, and κRef(c)\kappa_{\mathrm{Ref}}(c)κRef​(c) if Mc′M'_cMc′​ or αc\alpha_cαc​ changed. If the child machine and its contract are fixed, κRef(c)\kappa_{\mathrm{Ref}}(c)κRef​(c) is unchanged as well.

The universal wiring-adequacy certificate is keyed by (Cv,Kv,αv,(αc)c,Γv,(Γc)c)(C_v,K_v,\alpha_v,(\alpha_c)_c,\Gamma_v,(\Gamma_c)_c)(Cv​,Kv​,αv​,(αc​)c​,Γv​,(Γc​)c​) and does not mention the child tuple. The instance Beh⁡exec(v)⊆Kv({αc(Beh⁡exec(c))}c)\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(v) \subseteq K_v(\{\alpha_c(\operatorname{Beh}_{\mathrm{exec}}(c))\}_c)Behexec​(v)⊆Kv​({αc​(Behexec​(c))}c​) is re-derived by applying the unchanged certificate to the new child behaviors; no ancestor solver is re-run. If a child interface map changes, the parent’s wiring-adequacy key changes and the applicable wiring evidence must be re-established; the zero-ancestor-solver cutoff assumes the family (αc)c(\alpha_c)_c(αc​)c​ is fixed. If a wiring cannot establish the universal certificate, its evidence is instance-specific; the cutoff claim does not apply to that ancestor, and the affected operational obligation is revalidated.

Proof. The keys are functions of their listed arguments. The parent keys list MvM_vMv​, WvW_vWv​, Bv,cB_{v,c}Bv,c​, αv\alpha_vαv​, Γv\Gamma_vΓv​, and the wiring (Cv,Kv,αv,(αc)c,Γv,(Γc)c)(C_v,K_v,\alpha_v,(\alpha_c)_c,\Gamma_v,(\Gamma_c)_c)(Cv​,Kv​,αv​,(αc​)c​,Γv​,(Γc​)c​); none lists Mc′M'_cMc′​ or the child behavior tuple. The sibling keys list their own children and contracts; none lists Mc′M'_cMc′​. The child’s own keys may change, including κImpl\kappa_{\mathrm{Impl}}κImpl​ for a changed leaf; κRef(c)\kappa_{\mathrm{Ref}}(c)κRef​(c) changes only if Mc′M'_cMc′​ or αc\alpha_cαc​ changes. Equal keys denote the same proposition, and the stored evidence proves that proposition; substituting the new child’s refinement proof into the parent’s derivation is sound by Theorem 2. ■\blacksquare■

The theorem does not require the new child to refine the old child. {0}\{0\}{0} and {1}\{1\}{1} are incomparable implementations of the same boundary {0,1}\{0,1\}{0,1}, and either may replace the other when the boundary is unchanged. The persistent store realizes the cutoff with path copying: the ancestor spine is rewritten, the unmodified subtrees are shared, and no ancestor solver is re-run.

7.4 The evolution loop

Section titled “7.4 The evolution loop”

The evolution function

Gt+1=evolve⁡(Gt,ΔI)G_{t+1} = \operatorname{evolve}(G_t, \Delta I)Gt+1​=evolve(Gt​,ΔI)

returns one of three outcomes: Verified, Conflict, or Unresolved. There is no default-to-pass.

Step 1 — Apply and reactivate. Apply ΔI\Delta IΔI: a new intent, a new decision, a protected revision with authorization, or a contract change. Recompute the active intents AkA_kAk​ top-down. Resolve the affected decisions and check consistency. Mark stale decisions by reverse reachability. If a nogood is fully selected, return Conflict with the minimal nogood and its supporting decisions; stop before any machine search.

Step 2 — Locate. Walk the layers from the root downward, checking the affected obligation keys. The result of each check is one of: pass, fail with a semantic counterexample, failed proof witness (for example, an inductive invariant or simulation relation that failed), or unresolved (timeout or unknown). Let jjj be the first layer at which an affected obligation does not pass. Do not take the Verified path merely because no obligation “fails”: publish only when every required obligation in the affected cone has valid pass evidence. A missing, unresolved, or pending obligation is not a pass.

Step 3 — Repair at jjj. The check result determines the repair:

  • Semantic counterexample, genuine. A concrete execution admitted by the failing layer’s machine violates an active intent, or a concrete interleaving of its children violates the decomposition. Repair the machine, connector, or contracts at that layer; re-establish its obligations and its refinement to the layer above; propagate upward only along the affected spine.
  • Semantic counterexample, spurious child refinement. The child’s model or abstraction overapproximates: it admits behavior the fixed child implementation cannot realize. Repair the child model or its abstraction map by narrowing the abstraction, and re-establish the lower realization and the upper refinement. Narrowing the parent’s incoming contract for a fixed child abstraction makes the inclusion harder and cannot remove the spurious behavior; reserve contract narrowing for the decomposition case below.
  • Semantic counterexample, spurious decomposition. The parent-side child contract is too permissive and the concrete children satisfy a stronger contract. Narrow the parent-side child contract or repair the connector, and re-establish the decomposition. If the concrete children do not satisfy the stronger contract, the repair belongs to the children, not to the contract.
  • Failed proof witness. An inductive invariant or simulation relation failed. Repair the witness (strengthen the invariant or relation) and recheck. This is a proof-search outcome, not a semantic counterexample and not a machine or contract edit by itself.
  • Unresolved. The checker timed out or returned unknown. Return Unresolved; do not classify it as genuine or spurious, and do not publish.

For a refinement failure, the set example is decisive: implementation {ok}\{ok\}{ok}, child abstraction {ok,bad}\{ok,bad\}{ok,bad}, parent contract {ok}\{ok\}{ok}. The implementation satisfies the contract, but the abstraction admits badbadbad. No stronger parent contract repairs the fixed child abstraction; narrowing the child abstraction to {ok}\{ok\}{ok} does. A child refinement failure is never repaired by strengthening the parent-side contract alone.

The genuine/spurious test for a semantic decomposition counterexample uses one shared trajectory:

∃r. legal⁡Wv(r) ∧ obs⁡v(r)=τ ∧ ∀c. realizable⁡(Mc,slice⁡c(r)).\exists r.\ \operatorname{legal}_{W_v}(r) \ \wedge\ \operatorname{obs}_v(r) = \tau \ \wedge\ \forall c.\ \operatorname{realizable}\bigl(M_c, \operatorname{slice}_c(r)\bigr).∃r. legalWv​​(r) ∧ obsv​(r)=τ ∧ ∀c. realizable(Mc​,slicec​(r)).

A separate existential trajectory per child is not sufficient. Two children can each be realizable on their own slice while no common trajectory exists. The shared-bit witness is Proposition 2.

Step 4 — Publish. If every obligation in the affected cone has valid pass evidence and every load-bearing decision is warranted, atomically advance the head from GtG_tGt​ to Gt+1G_{t+1}Gt+1​ and record the authorization. Otherwise return Unresolved with the failing or unresolved obligations and their witnesses.

7.5 Genuine vs. spurious

Section titled “7.5 Genuine vs. spurious”

Proposition 2 (Separate realizations do not imply a joint realization). There are two child contracts, one requiring a shared bit to be 000 and one requiring it to be 111, such that each is separately realizable but no common trajectory realizes both.

Proof. Let the shared bit be b∈{0,1}b \in \{0,1\}b∈{0,1}. Child 1 is realizable only with b=0b = 0b=0; child 2 is realizable only with b=1b = 1b=1. Each existential check succeeds with a different value of bbb. No single rrr has b=0b = 0b=0 and b=1b = 1b=1. ■\blacksquare■

The proposition is the reason the repair step uses a joint trajectory. It is also the reason a connector that hides shared state behind per-child contracts is unsound: the correlation is not in either contract.

7.6 Staleness and reopening

Section titled “7.6 Staleness and reopening”

A change to an intent, contract, or decision activates the dependency cone. Every decision in the cone is stale until re-warranted. A reopened alternative becomes selectable again; selecting it is a new decision with its own prerequisites and evidence. The prior selection remains in the history, so the audit trail is not rewritten.

The dependency cone is computed on the reference graph, not on the storage graph. A subtree storage change with an unchanged semantic contract does not activate the cone; a semantic change with an unchanged storage pointer does. This is the practical benefit of separating keys from pointers.
